title: Site checks and social stats: two requests for one new address at once pay for one check, not two — a row a worker finished after the caller looked is not queued again
steps: S1: two web instances receive /site-checks for the same new address at the same moment; the first instance's tick claims and finishes the row before the second instance writes its enqueue.
S2: a durable-queue row was finished at T+1 s; enqueue is called with seenAt = T, then with seenAt = T+2 s.
S3: /social-stats with force for a profile finished a moment ago.
expect: S1: both callers are told queued, one row exists, the address is fetched once (CI 19/10 run 39218… failed this with 'checked once: 2 !== 1').
S2: the first enqueue leaves the row done with its fields; the second re-queues it.
S3: force still queues: seenAt is not applied to a forced refresh.
evidence: Tracy CI on PR #1446 (head ac9e9e197a), job 'build check (tests 1/2)' 19/10/2026 08:12Z: website-opportunities-site-checks.test.mjs:467 'two callers asking for the same new address at once make one row, both told queued' → AssertionError checked once 2 !== 1; the race the A0 agent left open on #1440 (request reads, worker finishes, request re-queues a fresh row)
fence: createDurableQueue.enqueue(entries, {seenAt}) adds `and (checked_at is null or checked_at < seenAt)` to the conditional upsert; site-checks.request and social-stats.request take seenAt before reading their rows and pass it (social-stats: not for force)

tests: enqueue with `seenAt` leaves a row a worker finished after the caller looked
two callers asking for the same new address at once make one row, both told queued
only the first `limit` unknown profiles are queued; force re-queues a fresh one
